history.caveat: No source tells this life: every particular of it is ours.
paragraphs: His family is put with the villages of the St. Joseph, on the St. Joseph River, east round the lake (three or four villages in May 1812), one of the bands of the Chicago country Governor Edwards described that spring.
He is of the Turkey gens (Pen′-nă), and his children are of it after him.
He has a pony, and some winters went as far as the Wabash to hunt.
He came in when the bands gathered at Chicago in August, and on the 13th was given cloth and blankets when the goods were handed out.

paragraphs: Her family is put with the villages of the St. Joseph, on the St. Joseph River, east round the lake (three or four villages in May 1812), one of the bands of the Chicago country Governor Edwards described that spring.
She is of the Black Hawk gens (M′-ke-tash′-she-kă-kah′); her husband, since no one married within the gens, is of another, and her children are of his.
She planted and hoed the village's corn, beans and squash in the spring, and made the rush and cattail mats the lodges here are covered with.
She came in when the bands gathered at Chicago in August, and on the 13th was given cloth and blankets when the goods were handed out.
